cards.front: Complete the rule: Before driving, decide whether you are.
cards.back: Before driving, decide whether you are physically and mentally able to drive safely.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver is responsible for making.
cards.back: A driver is responsible for making sure the vehicle is safe to operate.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Routine vehicle maintenance should follow the owner’s manual.
cards.back: Routine vehicle maintenance should follow the owner’s manual, with work beyond the driver’s ability handled by a qualified mechanic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Brake noise, an unusual brake smell or a.
cards.back: Brake noise, an unusual brake smell or a brake pedal reaching the floor calls for a mechanic’s inspection.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check turn signals, brake lamps, taillamps and headlights.
cards.back: Check turn signals, brake lamps, taillamps and headlights from outside the vehicle to confirm that they work.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Brake lamps communicate that.
cards.back: Brake lamps communicate that the vehicle is stopping.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Turn signals communicate.
cards.back: Turn signals communicate an intended turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Using headlights during both daylight and.
cards.back: Using headlights during both daylight and darkness helps other drivers see the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Have a mechanic check headlight alignment if seeing.
cards.back: Have a mechanic check headlight alignment if seeing at night is difficult or other drivers frequently flash their headlights at you.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Trip planning can reduce driving by combining.
cards.back: Trip planning can reduce driving by combining errands, sharing rides or using available public transportation.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Avoiding heavy traffic reduces wear.
cards.back: Avoiding heavy traffic reduces wear on the driver and vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before a pickup trip, call to confirm.
cards.back: Before a pickup trip, call to confirm the needed item is available or ready.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Replace damaged windshield glass because it can obstruct.
cards.back: Replace damaged windshield glass because it can obstruct sight and break more easily in a minor collision or impact.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Replace ineffective wiper blades so the windshield.
cards.back: Replace ineffective wiper blades so the windshield can be cleared of rain and snow.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Remove snow and ice.
cards.back: Remove snow and ice from every window before driving.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping.
cards.back: Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distance and make turning harder on wet roads.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Low tire pressure or unbalanced tires can increase.
cards.back: Low tire pressure or unbalanced tires can increase wear and fuel use while making steering and stopping harder.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling.
cards.back: Bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side warrants a mechanic’s check.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Worn tires can cause hydroplaning and.
cards.back: Worn tires can cause hydroplaning and increase the likelihood of a blowout.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use a gauge to check pressure while the.
cards.back: Use a gauge to check pressure while the tires are cold, using the owner’s manual to find the recommended pressure.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For the penny tread check, insert Lincoln’s head.
cards.back: For the penny tread check, insert Lincoln’s head first; if the tread does not reach at least his head, replace the unsafe tire.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Have a mechanic inspect steering that is hard.
cards.back: Have a mechanic inspect steering that is hard to turn or does not respond when the steering wheel first turns.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Excessive bouncing or continued bouncing after a bump.
cards.back: Excessive bouncing or continued bouncing after a bump or stop is a reason for a mechanic to inspect the suspension.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The exhaust system removes engine gases, reduces.
cards.back: The exhaust system removes engine gases, reduces engine noise and cools the hot exhaust.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Leaking exhaust fumes can quickly be.
cards.back: Leaking exhaust fumes can quickly be fatal and can make a driver drowsy.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not run a.
cards.back: Do not run a vehicle’s engine inside a garage.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook warns against sitting in a car.
cards.back: The handbook warns against sitting in a car with its engine running without an open window.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Have exhaust leaks repaired.
cards.back: Have exhaust leaks repaired when they are detected.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A poorly tuned engine may lose needed.
cards.back: A poorly tuned engine may lose needed power, fail to start or stall in traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Secure objects on the rear shelf or back.
cards.back: Secure objects on the rear shelf or back seat that could strike someone during a sudden stop or crash.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep floor objects from rolling under.
cards.back: Keep floor objects from rolling under the brake pedal and preventing braking.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Use the horn.
cards.back: Use the horn only to warn others.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six.
cards.back: For vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six, the listed front lighting must be white or amber and the rear lighting red or amber, visible from five hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Headlights and taillights must not be tinted or.
cards.back: Headlights and taillights must not be tinted or covered with colored material unless compliant original or optional equipment meets federal manufacturing regulations.

cards.front: Complete the rule: High-beam headlights should reveal people or.
cards.back: High-beam headlights should reveal people or vehicles at three hundred fifty feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Low-beam headlights should reveal people.
cards.back: Low-beam headlights should reveal people or vehicles at one hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Dim high beams when an approaching.
cards.back: Dim high beams when an approaching vehicle is one thousand feet away.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When overtaking another vehicle, dim.
cards.back: When overtaking another vehicle, dim high beams at five hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Headlights must be used from half an hour.
cards.back: Headlights must be used from half an hour after sunset until half an hour before sunrise.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Headlights are required when weather or blowing.
cards.back: Headlights are required when weather or blowing dust reduces visibility below five hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Flashing or pulsating vehicle lights other than turn.
cards.back: Flashing or pulsating vehicle lights other than turn signals are prohibited unless the vehicle is authorized or an emergency vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Decorative undercarriage lights must not rotate, flash, oscillate.
cards.back: Decorative undercarriage lights must not rotate, flash, oscillate or use a color reserved for police or emergency vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six.
cards.back: On vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six, turn signals must show white or amber ahead and red or amber behind, visible for three hundred feet in sunlight.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Signal lamps are required if the steering-post center.
cards.back: Signal lamps are required if the steering-post center is more than twenty-four inches from the vehicle’s left edge or more than fourteen feet from the rear edge of the vehicle or load.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Brake lamps indicate.
cards.back: Brake lamps indicate slowing or stopping.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For vehicles built after January one, nineteen fifty-six.
cards.back: For vehicles built after January one, nineteen fifty-six, brake lights must be red or amber and visible from three hundred feet in normal sunlight.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A vehicle made after January one, nineteen fifty-six.
cards.back: A vehicle made after January one, nineteen fifty-six must have white license-plate illumination visible for fifty feet behind it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: License-plate lighting that is not.
cards.back: License-plate lighting that is not original manufacturer equipment is prohibited.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The muffler must prevent.
cards.back: The muffler must prevent unusual or excessive noise.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A vehicle manufactured after January one, nineteen fifty-six.
cards.back: A vehicle manufactured after January one, nineteen fifty-six must provide a rearward mirror view of two hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The service and parking brakes must control, stop.
cards.back: The service and parking brakes must control, stop and hold the vehicle for its operating loads and grades.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The horn must be.
cards.back: The horn must be audible from two hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When headlamps are required, a vehicle stopped or.
cards.back: When headlamps are required, a vehicle stopped or parked on a roadway must show parking lights that are white or amber ahead and red behind, visible for five hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Motor vehicles require a front windshield, with safety.
cards.back: Motor vehicles require a front windshield, with safety glass required for those manufactured after January one, nineteen fifty-six.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The windshield must stay in a condition.
cards.back: The windshield must stay in a condition that does not block the driver’s view.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not attach material to any.
cards.back: Do not attach material to any window if it restricts the driver’s view.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Working windshield wipers are required to.
cards.back: Working windshield wipers are required to remove rain, snow and other moisture.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Vehicles manufactured between January one, nineteen sixty-five and.
cards.back: Vehicles manufactured between January one, nineteen sixty-five and January one, nineteen sixty-eight must have belts for both outer front seats.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Vehicles manufactured after January one, nineteen sixty-eight.
cards.back: Vehicles manufactured after January one, nineteen sixty-eight require seatbelts at every designated seating position.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Seatbelts must be.
cards.back: Seatbelts must be kept in working order.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver may not drive in Montana unless.
cards.back: A driver may not drive in Montana unless each occupant has a properly adjusted and fastened safety belt.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For buses and trucks over eighty inches wide.
cards.back: For buses and trucks over eighty inches wide, and trailers or semitrailers over three thousand pounds gross vehicle weight and over that width, two clearance lamps are required at the front and two at the rear, one on each side.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A truck tractor needs two front.
cards.back: A truck tractor needs two front clearance lamps, one on each side.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A pole trailer above three thousand pounds gross.
cards.back: A pole trailer above three thousand pounds gross vehicle weight needs a clearance lamp on each side.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six need.
cards.back: Vehicles made after January one, nineteen fifty-six need two rear taillamps, except motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, quadricycles and truck tractors.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Clearance lamps must be amber at the front.
cards.back: Clearance lamps must be amber at the front or side and red at the rear, and visible for five hundred feet when required.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A load projecting at least four feet beyond.
cards.back: A load projecting at least four feet beyond the vehicle body needs a red lamp at its farthest rear point, visible for five hundred feet, while headlamps are required.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When headlamps are not required, a load extending.
cards.back: When headlamps are not required, a load extending four feet or more beyond the vehicle body needs a red flag at least twelve inches square.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A farm tractor or implement of husbandry moving.
cards.back: A farm tractor or implement of husbandry moving on a highway during required-headlamp hours must show a front white light visible for at least five hundred feet and a rear red light visible for five hundred feet.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Required farm-vehicle lights must be mounted.
cards.back: Required farm-vehicle lights must be mounted to show the vehicle’s farthest left projection.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A vehicle may carry no more.
cards.back: A vehicle may carry no more than two spot or auxiliary fog lamps.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Turn spot lamps off when approaching.
cards.back: Turn spot lamps off when approaching another moving vehicle from either direction.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Fog lamps may accompany low-beam headlights only if.
cards.back: Fog lamps may accompany low-beam headlights only if the fog-lamp beam is no stronger than the low beam.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Trailers, semitrailers and pole trailers need separation-activated break-away.
cards.back: Trailers, semitrailers and pole trailers need separation-activated break-away brakes if they have air or vacuum brakes or weigh more than three thousand pounds gross.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Maintain brakes in working order and adjust.
cards.back: Maintain brakes in working order and adjust them to act equally on all wheels.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Vehicle sirens, whistles and bells are prohibited except.
cards.back: Vehicle sirens, whistles and bells are prohibited except where authorized emergency vehicles are permitted to use them.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A trailer, semitrailer or pole trailer weighing three.
cards.back: A trailer, semitrailer or pole trailer weighing three thousand pounds gross vehicle weight or less needs a securely fastened front steel safety chain or cable at least one-quarter inch in diameter.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A truck with at least one-ton capacity, passenger.
cards.back: A truck with at least one-ton capacity, passenger bus or truck tractor must carry the specified warning equipment.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Three emergency reflective triangles meeting United States Department.
cards.back: Three emergency reflective triangles meeting United States Department of Transportation Motor Vehicles Safety Standard one hundred twenty-five may replace the listed warning-device set.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Vehicles carrying explosives, flammable liquids or compressed gases.
cards.back: Vehicles carrying explosives, flammable liquids or compressed gases, or using compressed gas fuel, must not carry flame-producing warning devices.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a truck, passenger bus, tractor, trailer, semitrailer.
cards.back: If a truck, passenger bus, tractor, trailer, semitrailer or pole trailer is disabled on a highway or shoulder while lamps are required, place an initial warning device immediately on the traffic side toward approaching traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For the listed disabled vehicles on an undivided.
cards.back: For the listed disabled vehicles on an undivided highway during required-lamp hours, warning devices go one hundred feet behind and one hundred feet ahead in the occupied lane, plus a traffic-side device at least ten feet toward the nearest approaching traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For the listed disabled vehicles on a divided.
cards.back: For the listed disabled vehicles on a divided highway during required-lamp hours, use the two hundred-foot rear placement and place the other lane device one hundred feet in the same direction instead of in front.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When a listed disabled vehicle is within five.
cards.back: When a listed disabled vehicle is within five hundred feet of a curve, hill or other blocked view, put the warning in that direction at least five hundred feet from the vehicle so approaching traffic has adequate warning.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When the stated lamp-time warning-device requirement does not.
cards.back: When the stated lamp-time warning-device requirement does not apply to a listed disabled vehicle on a roadway, the driver must display two red flags at the specified front and rear positions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In the stated highway or shoulder disablement situations.
cards.back: In the stated highway or shoulder disablement situations, a vehicle carrying explosives, flammable liquid or compressed gas, or using compressed gas fuel, needs immediate red electric-lantern or portable-red-reflector warnings on its traffic side and one hundred feet ahead and behind in its occupied lane.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not use flares, fuses or other flame.
cards.back: Do not use flares, fuses or other flame signals to warn of a disabled vehicle carrying explosives, flammable liquids or compressed gases, or using compressed gas as fuel.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A slow-moving vehicle or item of equipment, animal-drawn.
cards.back: A slow-moving vehicle or item of equipment, animal-drawn vehicle, or road-work machine normally operating at twenty-five miles per hour or less needs the rear emblem, except machinery doing actual road work while protected by a flagger or warning signs.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The slow-moving emblem is a fluorescent yellow-orange.
cards.back: The slow-moving emblem is a fluorescent yellow-orange triangle with a fourteen-inch base and fourteen-inch height.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The slow-moving emblem needs reflective red.
cards.back: The slow-moving emblem needs reflective red border stripes one and three-quarter inches wide.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Mount the slow-moving emblem at the rear.
cards.back: Mount the slow-moving emblem at the rear center, three to five feet above the road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: On a two-lane road, a slow vehicle that.
cards.back: On a two-lane road, a slow vehicle that leaves no clear passing lane must pull over at the first safe opportunity with sufficient turnout space to let others pass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep the windshield clean because sunlight or.
cards.back: Keep the windshield clean because sunlight or headlights on dirty glass can make seeing difficult.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Keep washer fluid filled and use antifreeze.
cards.back: Keep washer fluid filled and use antifreeze washer fluid where temperatures may drop below freezing.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Clean interior window surfaces, especially.
cards.back: Clean interior window surfaces, especially when smoking has left a film.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Before driving, clear snow, ice and frost.
cards.back: Before driving, clear snow, ice and frost from the front, side and rear windows.
